title: It was a great week for innovation across the model ecosystem. We’re bringing these new models into Copilot, enabling it to take on increasingly complex work, from quick questions to delegated tasks and, increasingly, complete long-running jobs through Autopilots. [Read more]
summary: It was a great week for innovation across the model ecosystem. We're bringing these new models into Copilot, enabling it to take on increasingly complex work, from quick questions to delegated tasks and, increasingly, complete long-running jobs through Autopilots. Here's one fun example: using an Opal-powered Autopilot running on a secure Windows 365 Cloud PC, Copilot goes through a month of trail cam footage, finds every animal sighting, creates a highlight reel of the best clips, labels each one with the camera, date, and species, catalogs every sighting in a spreadsheet, builds a PowerPoint summarizing the findings, and shares everything in Teams for colleagues to review. This is the next frontier for Copilot: software that doesn't just assist with work, but can own and complete entire tasks that unfold over hours or days. Learn more about Opal, the technology powering one of these new Autopilot experiences (in Frontier rings now and coming to Copilot soon): https://lnkd.in/grsmeiNt | 281 comments on LinkedIn

The teams that get value from Autopilots should be able to define what a reviewable output looks like before they switch one on. It all lands in Teams: a month of footage becomes a highlight reel, a spreadsheet and a deck, and someone still has to decide whether the species labels are right. Long-running jobs shift the work from producing to checking, and checking a day of autonomous output is harder than checking a diff, because you’re reconstructing what it did rather than reading what changed. Very exciting!!

[Harish Purohit](https://in.linkedin.com/in/harish-purohit?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 2d


As we have witnessed the journey of ChatGpt and Copilot, The real shift isn’t from “AI that assists” to “AI that automates.” It’s from AI that responds to work → AI that takes ownership of work. What’s especially interesting here is the ability to handle a task end-to-end across multiple tools, decisions, and hours of execution—not just generate an answer in seconds. That could fundamentally change how we think about productivity, software, and even what a “job” looks like. The next question isn’t “What can AI help me do?” It’s “What work can I confidently hand over to AI?”
